edition.locus: Against Marcion 3.3 (signs alone insufficient; Creator’s prior works)

source_text: \'Non fuit\', inquis, \'ordo eiusmodi necessarius, quia statim se et filium et missum et dei Christum rebus ipsis esset probaturus per documenta uirtutum\'. at ego negabo solam hanc illi speciem ad testimonium competisse, quam et, ipse postmodum exauctorauit. siquidem edicens multos uenturos et signa facturos et uirtutes magnas edituros (ad) auersionem etiam electorum, nec ideo tamen admittendos, temerariam signorum et uirtutum fidem ostendit, ut etiam apud pseudochristos facillimarum. aut quale est, si inde se uoluit probari et intellegi et recipi, ex uirtutibus dico, unde ceteros noluit, aeque et ipsos tam subito uenturos quam a nullo auctore praedicatos? si quia prior eis uenit et prior uirtutum documenta signauit, idcirco, quasi locum in balneis, ita fidem occupauit, posteris quibusque praeripuit, uide, ne et ipse in condicione posteriorum deprehendatur, posterior inuentus creatore, ante iam cognito et proinde uirtutes ante operato et non aliter praefato non esse aliis credendum, post eum scilicet. igitur si priorem uenisse et priorem de posteris pronuntiasse hoc fidem t cludet, praedamnatus erit et ipse iam ab eo, quo posterior est agnitus, et solius erit auctoritas creatoris hoc in posteros constituendi, qui nullo posterior * non potuit. iam nunc, cum probaturus sim creatorem easdem uirtutes, quas solas ad fidem Christo tuo uindicas, interdum per famulos suos retro edidisse interdum per Christum suum edendas destinasse, possum et ex hoc merito praescribere tanto magis Christum (tuum) non ex solis uirtutibus credendum fuisse, quanto illum non alterius quam creatoris interpretari potuissent, ut respondentes uirtutibus creatoris et editis per famulos suos et in Christum suum repromissis. quamquam, et si alia documenta inuenirentur in tuo Christo, noua scilicet, facilius crederemus etiam noua eiusdem esse. cuius et uetera, quam cuius tantummodo noua, egentia experimentis fidei uictricis uetustatis, ut sic quoque praedicatus uenire debuerit tam praedicationibus propriis exstruentibus ei fidem quam et uirtutibus. praesertim aduersus Christum creatoris uenturus et signis et prophetiis propriis munitum, ut aemulus Christi per omnes diuersitatum species reluceret. sed quomodo a deo numquam praedicato Christus eius praedicaretur? hoc est ergo, quod exigis: nec deum nec Christum tuum credi, quia et deus ignotus esse non debuit et Christus agnosci per deum debuit.,
pass_a_gloss: Signa sola non fides (pseudochristi). Creator prior uirtutibus. Deus ignotus⇒Christus eius non praedicabilis.
pass_b_english: ‘There was no need,’ you say, ‘of such an order, because at once by the things themselves he would prove himself both Son and sent and God’s Christ through documents of powers.’ But I will deny that this species alone suited him for testimony—which he himself later also cashiered.

For when he announces many will come and do signs and put forth great powers even to the aversion of the elect, yet not for that to be admitted, he shows faith in signs and powers as rash—as easiest even among false Christs. Or what sort of thing is it if he wanted himself proved and known and received from powers—from where he did not want the others, themselves about to come as suddenly and as unpreached by any author?

If because he came before them and first sealed documents of powers, therefore, as if seizing a place at the baths, he occupied faith and snatched it from all later—see that he himself not be caught in the condition of the later, found later than the Creator, already known before and likewise working powers before and not otherwise foretelling that others after him must not be believed. Therefore if coming first and pronouncing first about later ones closes faith this way, he himself will already be prejudged by him than whom he is recognized later—and only the Creator’s authority will be for establishing this against later ones, who being later than none could not fail.

Already now, when I am about to prove the Creator formerly put forth through his servants the same powers you claim alone for faith in your Christ, and destined them to be put forth through his Christ, I can also from this rightly prescribe that your Christ all the more was not to be believed from powers alone, insofar as they could have been interpreted as of none other than the Creator—answering the Creator’s powers both done through servants and promised unto his Christ.

Though even if other—new—documents were found in your Christ, we would more easily believe even new things belong to him whose also the old are, than to him of only new things needing experiments of a faith that conquers antiquity—so that thus too he ought to have come preached, building faith by proper preachings as also by powers; especially about to come against the Creator’s Christ fortified by both signs and his own prophecies, that as rival of Christ he might shine through every species of diversities. But how would his Christ be preached from a god never preached? This then is what you demand: that neither your god nor your Christ be believed, because God ought not to be unknown and Christ ought to be known through God.
